main_text.p: logiæ propriis constant: ut Christus est Θεάνθρω-πος : Ecclesia est Catholica, & similes quas philoso-phia ne primoribus quidem labris attingere debet. Nam non licet μεταβαίνειν εἰς ἄλλο γένος.
vel Mixtæ.Mixtæ conclusiones sunt, quæ uno termino Theologico, altero philosophico combinantur.
Suntq; vel ex philosophiâ theoreticâ, vel practicâ,

Conclusiones mixtæ ex terminis Theologicis & philosophicis theoreticis sunt hæ: An attributa divina ab essentiâ & inter se differant re, vel ratione: & si ratione, an ratiocinante, vel ratiocinatâ? An in Deo differant esse & essentia? Quomodo personæ SS. Trinitatis ab essentiâ, & inter sese distinguantur? An accidentia panis & vini in Eucharistiâ per se possint subsistere? An ignis urat semper actu primo, vel secundo? Quomodo Christus Θεάνθρωπος fuerit in veteri Testamento? Quomodo vita æterna dicatur esse in nobis? Quomodo fides sit & non sit sine bonis operibus? Hic enim Theologus ex Metaphysico latifundio petit distinctionem inter essentiam & existentiam. E physicis autem terminis componuntur hæ conclusiones: Quomodo generatio & creatio differant? Quomodo materia prima Mosaica differat ab Aristotelica? An corpus Christi sit in loco? An cælum supremum sit in loco? Keckerm. præcogn. philos. l.1. cap. 4. & Syst. Logic. l.3. c.9. page.notes: The right edge strip (gen, con, pra, ... ) is the neighbouring page and was left out. Greek words were copied as printed; "Θεάνθρω-πος" is broken at the line end and the second half "πος" was read from the scan with some doubt. The italic/roman split of the conclusion list follows the visible type; the Keckerm. citation is set in roman inside the paragraph. The word "genus." at bottom right is treated as a catchword.
